forecast.event: official 10-year Treasury constant-maturity rate for 2026-08-20 is >=4.70%

benchmarks.name: no_change
benchmarks.note: Official 2026-08-19 10-year CMT; fixed prospectively at creation.

benchmarks.name: one_day_recent_trend
benchmarks.note: Mechanical continuation of the Aug. 18-to-Aug. 19 6 bp decline; fixed prospectively and not treated as a structural model.

original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Rates table for the official 2026-08-20 10-year CMT. Resolve the binary event TRUE if the published value is 4.70% or higher, otherwise FALSE. Score Brier and log loss. Score the 4.66% point estimate and fixed no-change/recent-trend point benchmarks by absolute error; record whether the 80% interval covers. Do not substitute an intraday market yield for the official CMT.
rationale: Treasury's Aug. 19 expansion of planned long-end liquidity-support buybacks adds a policy/liquidity channel that should reduce the probability of an immediate full rebound above 4.70% if the announcement effect persists.
The July FOMC minutes and WTI/Brent near four-week highs create an opposing upward-rate channel through inflation expectations and a more hawkish conditional policy reaction function.

The 4.70% event is set above the Aug. 19 official 4.65% close and receives below-even probability because the new long-end intervention signal is currently the strongest near-term rate-specific evidence, while uncertainty remains wide.
This forecast is intended to test persistence of the newly modeled policy/liquidity channel against renewed H003 inflation pressure, not to infer causation from one daily rate move.
surprising_if: The official 10-year CMT is >=4.80% without a major new inflation, geopolitical, issuance, or policy shock, implying rapid reversal of the Aug. 19 long-end relief.
The official 10-year CMT is <=4.52% without a major growth shock or additional policy intervention, implying substantially stronger easing than the model expects.

resolution.source: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, observation dated 2026-08-20: official 10-year CMT 4.69%, versus 4.65% on 2026-08-19.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved without hindsight alteration. The >=4.70% event resolved FALSE at 4.69%. The point estimate missed by 0.03 percentage point, the 80% interval covered, and the point forecast modestly beat both frozen point benchmarks. Because the outcome finished one basis point below the event threshold and one daily observation cannot identify the Treasury-buyback mechanism, this is scored as forecast performance only, not causal validation. Scored before post-cutoff evidence intake or model revision.
